question: Describe how the kingdom of Van Lang was organized under the Hung Kings.
key_points: National name Van Lang; capital Phong Chau (Bach Hac district)
15 administrative regions as vassal lands; Van Lang is the capital region
Civil generals Lac Hau; military generals Lac Tuong

ground_truth: Hung Vuong named the country Van Lang and set the capital at Phong Chau (Bach Hac district). The country was divided into 15 administrative regions, all vassal lands of Hung Vuong, with Van Lang the region of the capital. Civil generals were called Lac Hau and military generals Lac Tuong; the king's sons were Quan Lang and daughters Mi Nuong; officials in charge of affairs were Bo Chinh, a hereditary succession from father to son called phu dao; kings of all generations were called Hung Vuong.

question: Trace the legendary line from Kinh Duong Vuong to the first Hung Vuong and explain how the Bach Viet people originated.

ground_truth: Kinh Duong Vuong (Loc Tuc), son of De Minh and the daughter of Vu Tien, was enfeoffed to rule the South as the kingdom of Xich Quy. He married Than Long, daughter of Dong Dinh Quan, and fathered Lac Long Quan (Sung Lam). Lac Long Quan married Au Co, daughter of De Lai, who bore a hundred sons (from a hundred eggs), the ancestors of the Bach Viet. The couple separated: 50 children followed the mother to the mountains and 50 followed the father to the South, and the eldest son became Hung Vuong.

question: Describe the family background and ancestry of the Tay Son brothers as the document presents it.
key_points: Ancestors from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An, moved south by Lord Nguyen's forces (captured in 1653-1657 per one account; followed Lord Nguyen in 1655 per another) to Tuy Vien / Tay Son
Original surname Ho (descending from Ho Quy Ly per one source), changed to Nguyen

ground_truth: Per Vietnamese chronicles, the ancestors came from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An, and were captured by Lord Nguyen's army around 1653-1657 and resettled in Tuy Vien district, Hoai Nhon prefecture. Another account says the family originally bore the surname Ho (descending from Ho Quy Ly) and followed Lord Nguyen south in 1655; Ho Phi Tien married the only daughter of a wealthy merchant in Phu Lac, so the children took the mother's surname Nguyen. The father, Nguyen (Ho) Phi Phuc, traded betel and had 8 children including three sons Nhac, Hue and Lu; the mother was Nguyen Thi Dong.

question: What do the sources cited in the document say about the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu, and do they agree?
key_points: The document says the sources are inconsistent
Several Vietnamese chronicles: Nhac, then Lu, then Hue
Quy Nhon local tradition: Nhac 'Brother Two', Hue 'Uncle Three Thom', Lu 'Master Four' (Hue before Lu)
Western missionaries: Hue was Lu's younger brother (Lu 'Lord Seven', Hue 'Lord Eight')
Le Trong Ham: Nhac, Lu, two daughters, then Hue
ground_truth: They do not agree; the document itself calls the sources inconsistent. Several Vietnamese chronicles give the order Nhac, Lu, Hue. Local tradition in old Quy Nhon calls Nhac 'Brother Two', Hue 'Uncle Three Thom' and Lu 'Master Four', placing Hue before Lu. Western missionaries' letters make Hue the younger brother of Lu (Lu 'Lord Seven', Hue 'Lord Eight'). Le Trong Ham gives the order Nhac, Lu, two daughters, then Hue.
gold_spans: Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent
The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue
Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom)
Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother
Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue
notes: Cau mau thuan nguon: diem cao neu neu duoc ca viec cac nguon khong dong y lan noi dung tung nguon.
